chunk_map.heading: Name the rules, place the file (H1 + lede)
Phase 1: Name the rules from this session
Reject or rewrite the generic rule
Phase 2: Pick where the file fires
Wire the file in, check the wording
Phase 3: Name the automation shapes, don't build them
Read the shapes, hold the build

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a student hits an unresolved pronoun/noun mid-deck and loses the thread. Checked line 16's new clause ('The scrollback is the right source here...') under context flag: 'here' = the phase the student is running (in-chunk), 'the scrollback' is a session artifact the carve-out exempts by name ('the scrollback' listed in the carve-out's own examples) and is independently covered by the maintainer's Scrollback-ownership accept-note. 'two push-backs / a second-pass walk-down / an approval' (ch1) resolve both as session artifacts AND as verified real beats in the immediately-preceding push-back-on-the-plan.md. No unresolved pronoun/noun found across all 8 chunks; harm absent.

Harm: student can't locate a source named only by ambiguous position ('the opening lecture said'). No backward positional callback to another file exists in body. 'The next small lecture' (ch0, ch6) is a forward navigational pointer to the literal next deck item (module include-order), not a narrative callback requiring the student to already know its content — harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a named beat was cut/renamed and the reference now dangles. Verified against curriculum/exercises/push-back-on-the-plan.md (the immediately prior M2 exercise, per trainer-modules.md line 204-205): 'two push-backs' (Phase 3), 'a second-pass walk-down' (exact term, line 89 of that file), and 'an approval' (## Approve, line 113-115) all exist as real, current beats. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read (guess-before-reveal ordering)
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction present anywhere in this exercise; rule doesn't apply to this artefact shape.
Harm: a chunk that projects as a blank/context-dependent wait-state. Every chunk (incl. the shortest, ch2 and ch6, each 2 sentences) carries a self-standing claim. Harm absent.

Harm: header promises content the chunk body contradicts or omits. Checked each of the 6 non-lede/non-recap headers against its body — each matches (e.g. ch4 'check the wording' matches its 'Read the three rules back... push back and have Claude rewrite' bullet). Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-cadence caps (Not-X-Not-Y-Z, anaphora triples, self-grading superlatives, number+retraction, abstraction stacks, empty-leg verb triplets)
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a slide reads as machine-cadence rather than plain prose, or leaks a value-prop claim via self-grading superlative. Swept all 8 chunks for each sub-pattern: no triple-negation constructions, no anaphora/epistrophe triples, no self-grading superlatives (blocking sub-item — none found), no number+own-retraction (the 'three to five' / 'two or three' ranges are plain ranges, not a stated-then-hedged single number), no abstraction-noun stacks, no empty-leg verb triplets. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: repo-authorial jargon (compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, surface-as-noun, firing) projects on a wall the student reads as insider language. Checked 'fires'/'the file fires' (ch0 widget, ch3 header+body): this is ordinary engineering usage for when a context/config file is loaded/triggers (auto-load vs @import) — the exact mechanism the exercise is teaching — not the repo's internal compendium-firing metaphor; distinguishable by referent (a real CLAUDE.md load event, not 'this rule fires'). No instance of compendium/forcing function/beat/mood/surface-as-noun/Connections-as-proper-noun anywhere in body. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles only, lightly
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: bold overload trains the eye to skip past everything unbolded. Every chunk carries at most one bold span; the recurring **Prompt**/**Note** labels are confirmed standard widget chrome (present identically in author-test-strategy-skill.md, build-your-system.md, find-the-wrong-claims.md) alongside the maintainer-attested **Time:**/**What you do:**/**What you build:**/**The point:**/**What happened:** chrome. No bolded full sentences. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed Slides deck, not long-read
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: content invisible in the default Slides deck gets judged/edited as if students see it. This is a standard exercise file included under the module's .phase--exercise wrapper (per trainer-modules.md M2 item 5) — no phase-less orphan section introduced by this edit. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position computed, content ordinals linted
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: hand-numbered headers drift from deck-computed position, or an in-file 'Phase K' reference dangles. Phase 1/2/3 headers are consecutive; ch5's 'the .md file you saved in Phase 2' resolves to ch3's header. scripts/check-slide-numbering.js run project-wide: 'OK — 59 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.' Harm absent.
